source.title: Scaling Expert Language Models with Unsupervised Domain Discovery
source.authors: Suchin Gururangan; Margaret Li; M. Lewis; Weijia Shi; Tim Althoff; Noah A. Smith; Luke Zettlemoyer

record.tranche_reason: The study measures held-out perplexity across training-token budgets in a different language-model training setup, but does not fit or test power-law curves.
record.gate_note: The paper's own perplexity scaling sweeps bear on V1's training-token dimension. It does not test power-law fits, parameter-count or compute exponents, extrapolation from smaller runs, or a parameter/token compute-optimal split. The study also reports downstream classification results, but does not test whether downstream performance is predictable from scale or pretraining loss. Figure-only perplexity values are not numerically extractable from the supplied text.
record.test_reason: This is a method paper on C-BTM, sparse expert LMs trained from an OPT seed. The dense 1-cluster perplexity curves are only compute-matched baselines for the method. They come from continued training of a pretrained checkpoint, not from-scratch pretraining. Token budget is raised by growing the effective batch size at a fixed 10K steps, so tokens and batch size are confounded. No power-law form is fitted or claimed, and the values are figure-only. Scaling laws (Hoffmann et al.) are cited only in the introduction. No version's form, exponents, extrapolation or allocation is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that C-BTM beats compute-matched dense and MoE baselines, with gains growing with data and cluster count. They find the optimal cluster count rises with budget. They make no power-law scaling claims.
record.recipe_differences: Uses unsupervised corpus clustering, independently trains expert language models, and ensembles them for inference; does not fit the original scaling-law models.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and cluster count affect the results; the optimal cluster count is dataset- and compute-budget-dependent. The paper also reports sensitivity to inference temperature and top-k, outside the tested V1 token-scaling rows.

fits_no_version.finding: The perplexity-optimal number of C-BTM clusters rises with training-token budget; 16 clusters is best at 168B tokens on both C4 and S2ORC.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In cluster-specialised expert ensembles, the optimal expert count grows with the data/compute budget.

fits_no_version.finding: A 16-cluster C-BTM model (5.2B inference parameters) matches a 6.7B dense model's C4 perplexity with 3.5x fewer training FLOPs (Fig. 11). This is a method comparison.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse expert ensembles shift the compute-perplexity frontier relative to dense models.

record.problems: Perplexity sweeps are shown as plots without extractable numeric values in the supplied text; no power-law fitting or uncertainty for the relevant perplexity comparisons is reported. The authors note that their training schedule and batch-size choices may affect results and that the optimal cluster count is likely dataset-specific.
record.rows_left_out: No additional V1 rows retained: the other plotted cluster-count perplexity curves in Figures 5 and 7 are figure-only and do not provide extractable values or a stated power-law fit. Other experiments concern sparsity, training speed, downstream classification, or cluster quality rather than the versions tested here.

untested.parts: Power-law form of pretraining loss in parameters, tokens or compute. Only figure-only dense-baseline perplexity curves from continued training exist; no fit.
Downstream predictability from scale or loss. Table 1 compares a few models on few-shot classification but tests no scaling trend.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V1 'tested' status is reclassified. The dense curves are confounded baselines: continued training from OPT, tokens scaled by effective batch size at fixed steps, and multi-epoch S2ORC. They are figure-only and come with no fit, so they cannot support or challenge V1.

versions.untested_parts: Tests held-out perplexity over training-token budgets in C-BTM settings only. Does not fit or establish a power-law form, test parameter-count scaling, or isolate compute scaling when other factors are not bottlenecks.
